modelNotice: This knowledge pack is an educational, non-validated heuristic model. Scores are relative pattern-consistency values, not disease probabilities or diagnoses.

hypotheses.label: Acute GI irritation
hypotheses.description: A broad pattern bucket for short-term gastrointestinal upset, not a diagnosis.

hypotheses.label: Dietary reaction / intolerance
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with recent food change, appetite or GI changes.

hypotheses.label: Hairball / ingested material irritation
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with retching, vomiting, hairball history or possible ingested material.

hypotheses.label: Urinary tract problem
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with straining, frequent small urinations, blood or absent urine.

hypotheses.label: Systemic inflammation / infection
hypotheses.description: Broad pattern associated with fever, lethargy, appetite loss and multisystem signs.

hypotheses.label: Medication / treatment effect
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with recent medication or treatment exposure and subsequent changes.

hypotheses.label: Stress / environmental change
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with environmental change, hiding, appetite change or altered behavior.

hypotheses.label: Respiratory problem
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with abnormal respiratory effort or open-mouth breathing.

hypotheses.label: Toxin / foreign material exposure
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with known or possible toxin or foreign-object exposure.

hypotheses.label: Pain / injury
hypotheses.description: Pattern associated with trauma, severe pain, collapse or mobility changes.

hypotheses.label: Metabolic / endocrine pattern
hypotheses.description: Broad pattern associated with combinations such as increased appetite, increased thirst/urine output and weight change. Not a diagnosis.

hypotheses.label: Renal / hydration pattern
hypotheses.description: Broad pattern associated with changes in thirst, urine volume, appetite, weight and energy. Not a diagnosis.

urgencyRules.title: Breathing difficulty
urgencyRules.message: Difficulty breathing or open-mouth breathing in a cat warrants immediate veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Unable to urinate
urgencyRules.message: Inability to pass urine is an emergency.

urgencyRules.title: Collapse or seizure
urgencyRules.message: Collapse, unresponsiveness, or seizure activity warrants emergency veterinary care.

urgencyRules.title: Possible toxin exposure
urgencyRules.message: Known or suspected toxin exposure should be discussed with a veterinarian or animal poison service immediately.

urgencyRules.title: Blood observed
urgencyRules.message: Blood in vomit or stool can require urgent veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Straining to urinate
urgencyRules.message: Urinary straining can become life-threatening, particularly if little or no urine is produced.

urgencyRules.title: Repeated vomiting with lethargy
urgencyRules.message: Repeated vomiting together with lethargy or weakness warrants prompt veterinary assessment.

urgencyRules.title: Severe pain
urgencyRules.message: Severe or obvious pain warrants prompt veterinary assessment.
